inputs.root_cause: Event 326's own exact_next_action named ubl's remaining certification gates as the highest-leverage next tick, since ubl was the last of the 6 FF6 formats still lacking a full gate set (2/10). Completing it would mean every format has satisfied invariant #4 (the 10-item gate list) for the first time this mission.
inputs.obligation_targeted: Not an obligation-register entry -- product-goal.yaml's own separate 'completion_invariants' gate list. Built all 8 missing gates for ubl.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: All 10 gate files now exist under reports/certification/ubl/, matching every sibling format. While building the installed-wheel-gate, discovered packaging/python/package-matrix.yaml's own ubl entry had NEVER been migrated to the shipped format_factory.ubl namespace (still module_import=ubl, smoke_module=ubl.ubl_codec, no build_mode declared, defaulting to legacy_staging) -- unlike all 5 sibling FF6 formats, already build_mode=native_pyproject. This meant EVERY co-install proof this entire session (Events 322/324/325/326, all already committed) had been testing ubl's deprecated legacy shim, not the real, currently-developed package. Fixed the matrix entry to match the sibling template exactly. Result: ubl's own deep_import went from 16/18 passing (2 legacy-shim-specific failures) to 37/37 passing (0 failures) -- the shipped package has zero import problems. Re-ran the full 6-format co-install proof with the fix: genuinely 0 failures across all 146 submodules of all 6 formats combined, the first fully clean result this mission has ever produced. Retracted the now-inaccurate '2 pre-existing ubl findings' citation from all 5 sibling compatibility-gate.json files plus the program-wide ff6-six-format-co-install-gate.json.
inputs.regression_tier: ubl suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff, plus the package-install-proof/oracle/reproducible-build/performance/co-install tools' own pass/fail verdicts

execution_steps: 1. typing-gate: ran mypy --strict against src/python/ubl/src/format_factory/ubl/ -- 0 errors across 38 files.

2. security-gate: checked for pre-existing security test files BEFORE writing anything (the now-standard discipline after ora's own near-miss this session) -- found TWO: test_obligation_security_baseline.py (comprehensive UBL-SEC-001 proof, already blocking a broad forbidden-module set including importlib entirely) and test_obligation_namespace_shadowing_security.py. Read both, identified the same one narrow gap already found for nrrd (bare eval/exec/compile/__import__ builtin calls, invisible to import-based scanning), verified ubl's own source has zero such calls, and added tests/python/ubl/test_obligation_security_eval_exec_sweep.py as a new, distinctly-named file.

3. resource-gate: read security/limits.py and grepped every .enforce()/manual-limit-check call site in reader.py/writer.py -- found all 6 dimensions enforced (max_input_bytes with a bounded-read guard against unbounded stream buffering, max_xml_nodes, max_nesting_depth, max_entries, max_decompressed_bytes, max_output_bytes). Consolidated 3 already-passing node/depth/entries tests; honestly disclosed that max_input_bytes/max_decompressed_bytes/max_output_bytes are enforced in source but lack their own dedicated named test (real, working enforcement, just not independently proven to the same depth as the other 3 dimensions).

4. installed-wheel-gate: ran tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format ubl -- got build_mode=legacy_staging, module_import=ubl, version=0.1.0.dev0 (not the real 0.2.0.dev0), 2/18 deep_import failures. This did not match the expected shape (every sibling format shows build_mode=native_pyproject, module_import=format_factory.{fmt}). Investigated packaging/python/package-matrix.yaml directly and found ubl's own entry was the one FF6 format GAP-FORENSIC-001 never actually migrated -- it still had the pre-migration shape verbatim. Fixed it to the exact native_pyproject template every sibling entry already uses (build_mode, local_dependencies, module_import=format_factory.ubl, smoke test against format_factory.ubl.load). Re-ran: 37/37 deep imports PASS, version 0.2.0.dev0, wheel_sha256 now matches EXACTLY what reproducible-build.json and independent-repository-extraction-gate.json already recorded (both .venv-pinned from Event 324) -- this also RETRACTS a conclusion from Event 324's own independent-repository-extraction work, which had attributed a ubl wheel-digest mismatch to 'a build-environment interpreter-pinning inconsistency (system python vs .venv python)'. That theory was wrong; the real cause was this packaging-matrix staleness. Once the matrix entry points at the real source, all three tools agree regardless of interpreter.

5. independent-oracle-gate: ubl already had a real, pre-existing oracle package -- ran fresh, 5/5 PASS, D1 depth, no fix needed (confirmed this oracle path was never affected by the packaging-matrix bug, since it resolves its own module path independently via tools/oracle/enriched_generic.py's own ENRICHED_LOADERS entry, already correctly pointing at format_factory.ubl).

6. performance-gate: added benchmark_ubl() to tools/certification/performance_benchmark.py following the exact same pattern as benchmark_xliff()/benchmark_ora()/benchmark_nrrd(). Ran the full tool; reverted the other formats' own regenerated baseline files (pure timing noise) and kept only ubl's genuinely new output.

7. corpus-gate: found ubl's own _corpus-manifest.yaml (the 6-valid+1-invalid synthetic set, separate from Event 320's own 55-official-OASIS-sample manifest) had no per-sample sha256 -- computed and added them. Ran format_factory.ubl.load()/validate() against every sample and found a genuine, real discrepancy: the invalid sample (missing-mandatory.xml) parses successfully and validate() reports is_valid=True, contradicting the manifest's own prior, never-actually-verified 'error_detection_rate: 1/1' claim. Root-caused via validate()'s own docstring (full mandatory-cardinality validation 'remains a mandatory open obligation', UBL-VALIDATE-001, already confirmed genuinely large earlier this session) and corrected the manifest's own claim to 0/1 with a full explanation rather than silently leaving a false claim on record.

8. documentation-gate: the prior README (58 lines, 6 sections) was already reasonably accurate, unlike ora's/nrrd's own stale ones -- kept it, but found it documented only 12 of this package's own 142 exported symbols and omitted entire subsystems (code-list validation, digital signatures, document indexing/business-role queries, the official OASIS corpus from Event 320). Added 4 new sections and substantially expanded the Public API section. Verified all 10 code-block-imported symbols plus all 43 backtick-quoted Public-API-prose symbols exist via hasattr(). Executed the 'Quick start' example end-to-end; spot-verified the code-list/document-indexing/signature examples via direct API calls.

9. compatibility-gate: re-ran the 6-format co-install proof with the packaging-matrix fix in place -- 6/6 PASS, and for the first time this entire mission, GENUINELY 0 failures across all 146 submodules of all 6 formats combined (previously always '2 pre-existing, disclosed' ubl findings). Updated the program-wide reports/certification/ff6-six-format-co-install-gate.json with a full retraction section, and added a short retraction note to all 5 sibling formats' own compatibility-gate.json files (ipynb/safetensors/xliff/ora/nrrd) rather than leaving their own prior '2 unrelated findings' citations standing uncorrected.

10. Final full regression: ubl suite 1178 passed (was 1176 baseline, +2 eval/exec-sweep tests); 6-format suite 3940 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (was 3938). mypy --strict and ruff both clean on every changed file.
